_source: Recorded ABB TA522 (1SAP180400R0001) battery-holder page. Title renders as `TA522`; the ordering code appears in the body, so the type code and the catalog number differ. The page publishes almost nothing technical — description `Battery holder. Without lithium battery for PM5xx and PM56xx (TA522)`, brand `ABB`, sku `1SAP180400R0001` — and that emptiness is what makes it valuable: it is the lowest-yield page in the corpus, so anything else that appears is noise.

_notes.finish: Was `finish = "and"`. A bare conjunction is never a surface finish — a stopword that survived because the finish extractor had no value sanity gate (P0.2#8). The assertion keeps the field empty until a real value is found.
_notes.why: Second generic-path shape: identity must be confirmed on a page whose display name (TA522) is not the catalog number (1SAP180400R0001).
_notes.found_two_classes: Promoting this fixture produced four garbage attributes, both classes new. (1) ABB's Google Tag Manager snippet reached the text layer whole and was split into `j=d.createElement(s),dl=l!='dataLayer'?'&l='+l` = `'';j.async=true;j.src=`. (2) Marketing prose from an unrelated ABB product family was chopped into fake spec pairs: `Mounting = options, offering expanded`, `Voltage = ranges and enhanced environmental`, `Voltage = ranges and are optimized for VFD operation with an internally mounted shaft grounding ring for bearing`.
_notes.route_was_the_bug: The second class was not a gate problem. `extractDelimitedPlainTextSpecAttributes` is named for a delimiter it did not require — its pattern was `(label)\s*(?::|-)?\s+(value)`, delimiter optional — so any sentence containing two spec words became a pair. The value always ends right before the NEXT label word, which in prose is that phrase's head noun, so the captured value is structurally guaranteed to be a dangling modifier.
_notes.measured_before_changing: Probed across the cached-page corpus, the undelimited branch produced SEVEN pairs and all seven were prose. Carrying digits did not redeem them — `Voltage = range (100-250 V 50/60 Hz and DC), managing large control` has four numbers in it, which is why the first rule tried (require a digit or a capital) was not enough.
_notes.regression_suite_caught_the_overreach: The second attempt — reject any lowercase-initial undelimited value — broke Phoenix Contact, which legitimately publishes `Color white (RAL 9010)` with no delimiter. The rule that shipped tests sentence SHAPE instead (comma+gerund, full stop before a capital, digit-free clause joined by a function word): it rejects all seven prose pairs and keeps all four real values.
